title: Towards Intersectionality in Machine Learning: Including More Identities, Handling Underrepresentation, and Performing Evaluation
reasoning: The paper's core investigation is into the ethical and normative implications of technical choices made when incorporating intersectionality into machine learning. It critiques existing evaluation metrics for their ethical shortcomings, such as the potential to 'reify existing hierarchies amongst subgroups', and proposes new metrics and evaluation frameworks based on ethical considerations. This represents a substantial evaluation of the ethics embedded within machine learning fairness practices, going far beyond a cursory 'Ethical Considerations' section.
